'''James David Ford''' (born November 6, 1982) is an American politician, currently a member of the [[Indiana Senate]].<ref name=wxin>[https://fox59.com/2018/11/06/democrat-j-d-ford-becomes-first-lgbt-candidate-elected-to-indiana-general-assembly/ "Democrat J.D. Ford becomes first LGBT candidate elected to Indiana General Assembly"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181116010301/https://fox59.com/2018/11/06/democrat-j-d-ford-becomes-first-lgbt-candidate-elected-to-indiana-general-assembly/ |date=2018-11-16 }}. [[WXIN]], November 6, 2018.</ref> Elected in the 2018 elections, he represents Senate District 29 as a member of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]].<ref name=wxin/> He earned a bachelor's degree from [[University of Akron]] in criminal justice and political science and a master's degree in education from [[Purdue University Northwest]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nwitimes.com/news/local/govt-and-politics/elections/senate-democrats-seek-fair-redrawing-of-legislative-district-boundaries/article_2bfe71fe-7fb3-5fd6-ac04-27b70bb4ab2f.html|title=Senate Democrats seek fair redrawing of legislative district boundaries|last=Carden|first=Dan|website=Northwest Indiana Times|date=17 November 2020 |language=en|access-date=2021-09-12}}</ref> He was elected as the congressperson for [[Indiana's 5th congressional district]] in [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Indiana#District 5|2026]], defeating [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] incumbent [[Victoria Spartz]] in the general election.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-11-03 |title=Democrat J.D. Ford beats Spartz in major upset for Indiana House seat |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/6194526-jd-ford-upsets-victoria-spartz/ |access-date=2026-11-04 |website=Thehill.com |language=en-US|last=Vakil|first=Caroline }}</ref>

He was the first and, as of 2025, the only openly [[LGBT]] person elected to Indiana's state legislature.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.indianasenatedemocrats.org/senators/s29/|title=Senator J.D. Ford|website=Indiana Senate Democrats|language=en|access-date=2021-09-12}}</ref> After inauguration, he will be the first openly gay representative from Indiana to the [[United States House of Representatives]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Casey |date=2026-11-04 |title=Democrat J.D. Ford unseats Victoria Spartz in major upset for Indiana's 5th District • Indiana Capital Chronicle |url=https://indianacapitalchronicle.com/2026/11/03/democrat-j-d-ford-declared-win-over-victoria-spartz-in-major-upset-for-indianas-5th-district/ |access-date=2026-11-04 |website=Indiana Capital Chronicle |language=en-US}}</ref>

He first ran for [[Indiana Senate]] District 29 in 2014 and lost to Republican incumbent [[Mike Delph]] but won four years later in a rematch.

In November 2020, he was elected as the Caucus Chair of the [[Indiana Senate]] [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrats]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Smith|first=Brandon|date=2020-11-06|title=Sen. Greg Taylor Is First Black Leader Of Legislative Caucus In State History|url=https://www.wfyi.org/news/articles/sen-greg-taylor-is-first-black-leader-of-legislative-caucus-in-state-history|access-date=2021-01-03|website=WFYI Public Media|language=en-us}}</ref> For the 2024 legislative session, Senator Ford serves on the following committees: Education and Career Development (Ranking Minority Member), Elections (Ranking Minority Member), Ethics, Family and Children Services (Ranking Minority Member), Health and Provider Services, Local Government, and Rules and Legislative Procedure<ref name="insendems">{{Cite web |last=insendems |title=Senator J.D. Ford {{!}} District 29 |url=https://iga.in.gov/legislative/2024/legislators/legislator_jd_ford_1#committees |access-date=2024-06-17 |website=Indiana Senate Democrats |language=en-US}}</ref>

In addition to these committee assignments, Ford was an Interim Senate Minority Member of the Legislative Council.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Indiana General Assembly |url=https://iga.in.gov/legislative/2024/legislators/legislator_jd_ford_1#committees |access-date=2024-06-17 |website=iga.in.gov}}</ref>
